items.title: Qwen shipped a 27B FP8 multimodal model
items.oneliner: Qwen released a 27B FP8 multimodal model, making image-text deployment cheaper without the usual quantization accuracy hit.

items.title: Google open-sourced private AI inference tooling
items.oneliner: Google's HEIR compiler brings homomorphic encryption closer to usable AI inference, which matters if your roadmap includes regulated data.

items.title: Mixedbread pushed search toward specialized agents
items.oneliner: Mixedbread says Toast 1 hit 70% correctness on enterprise finance search, signaling narrower agents may beat general copilots.

items.title: Researchers exposed a Boeing 737 hacking path
items.oneliner: Researchers hacked a Boeing 737 with a coin-sized device in under a minute, proving physical access still breaks cyber assumptions.

items.title: Encryption is reshaping law enforcement tactics
items.oneliner: Strong default encryption is pushing law enforcement from wiretaps toward device hacking, and that policy fight is getting sharper.

items.title: Debian opened a formal vote on AI
items.oneliner: Debian started voting on AI and LLM contributions, a sign open source governance is moving from debate to enforceable policy.

items.title: RustDesk finally solved Wayland unattended access
items.oneliner: RustDesk added true unattended Wayland remote access, removing one of Linux desktop ops' most stubborn practical blockers.

items.title: TLA+ caught a production-grade distributed bug
items.oneliner: Depot used TLA+ to catch a distributed systems bug tests missed, which is your reminder that concurrency still punishes intuition.

items.title: Auto-research produced a 232x faster kernel
items.oneliner: A Codex-assisted workflow delivered a 232x faster GPU kernel, hinting that optimization work is becoming search, not craft.

items.title: Firefox became the last uBlock holdout
items.oneliner: Firefox is now the last major browser supporting full uBlock Origin, turning extension policy into a real platform differentiator.
